column62:
- Current age bracket: nominal age 1107 Ma, lomagage 1105 Ma, himagage 1109 Ma.
Heaman and Machado (1992) dated several centers by U-Pb (zircon/baddeleyite). The
**reversed-polarity** eastern gabbro (Center A) gives the most precise dates,
**1108 ± 1 Ma** and 1107 +5/−1 Ma, and the central nepheline syenite (Center C,
also reversed) gives a comparable 1109 +8/−4 Ma. The western granite — from the
western part of the complex, where the **normal-polarity** Center B sits — is
less well dated: its four zircon fractions give ²⁰⁷Pb/²⁰⁶Pb model ages of 1103–1090 Ma
and do not define a simple discordia; omitting one fraction, Heaman and Machado
(1992) assign it an upper-intercept age of 1107 +9/−5 Ma, and Kulakov et al. (2014)
note that it could be a few million years younger. Field relationships show the
western units intruding the other phases. The
geochronology is not precise enough to fully resolve the emplacement history, but
it indicates that the reversed Centers A and C are the older (~1108 Ma) rocks and
the normal western rocks are younger, bracketing the single normal/reversed
polarity reversal recorded by the complex to ~1102–1105 Ma.

The Coldwell pole (Centers A + C) averages reversed-polarity bodies that record
paleolatitudinal change within the Alona Bay reversed-polarity chron, so they need
not share a single age. The pole is therefore assigned the midpoint of 1105–1109 Ma,
an interval spanning the dates of the eastern gabbro (1108 ± 1 Ma) and the central
nepheline syenite (1109 +8/−4 Ma), rather than the 1108 ± 1 Ma date of the eastern
gabbro alone, which Kulakov et al. (2014, Table 4) assign to it.
